subject: VPC bundling & support concession — request for structured credit
messages:
From: Toby Chen <toby.chen@hearthwell.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 15:12:23 -0800
Subject: Packaging & credits question for VPC deployment

Hi Grace / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look promising. We're getting internal pushback on the platform fee line item when comparing to other vendors' "all-in" offers. Two asks from procurement: (1) can Redwood amortize the platform fee across the first 12 months as a structured credit (rather than a large upfront invoice), and (2) is there flexibility to convert a portion of the implementation retainer into time-limited credits against overage support?

High level: 4-node private VPC, 24/7 priority SRE (P1/P2), target go-live by end of Q1. I attached our security/MPA note — procurement wants a clear path to keep cash impact low in year one.

Can you share a counter proposal and any internal approval constraints we should know about?

Best,
Toby Chen
Head of Platform Engineering | Hearthwell Systems
T: +1 415 555 0198

Attachments: hearthwell-mpa-requirements.pdf (pdf, 410KB)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>
To: Toby Chen <toby.chen@hearthwell.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 18:04:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging & credits question for VPC deployment

Hi Toby — appreciate the clear asks. Short answer: yes, we can structure a 12-month amortization of the platform fee as a monthly credit schedule for year one, and we can propose converting up to 50% of the implementation retainer into time-limited support credits (valid for 12 months post-go-live).

I'll loop in Pricing and Finance internally to confirm exact numbers and any approval matrix items. In the meantime, can you confirm the committed monthly token baseline (so we can size the credit against expected consumption) and whether the 24/7 SRE is a hard requirement or whether a blended P1/P2 on-call with an uptime SLA would suffice for a starter pilot?

Quick next step: Marissa will send a counter with two options (pilot-friendly and enterprise anchor) — we aim to keep the commercial decision simple so procurement can move quickly.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: Hearthwell concession sizing (RDW-2026-1193)

Team — quick internal note before I draft the customer-facing counter. Key points from procurement: amortize platform fee over 12 months; convert implementation retainer -> support credits (up to 50%); want minimal upfront cash. They are targeting 4 dedicated nodes, monthly baseline ~120M tokens. Pilot go-live EoQ1.

Options I propose:
- Option A (Pilot-friendly): 40% of platform fee credited evenly across 12 months (applied as monthly invoice credit), implementation retainer: 30% converted to support credits (12-month expiration), standard P1/P2 SRE (no 24/7 escalation hours included) — revenue impact: ~12% ARR concession first year; requires AE + RevOps approval.
- Option B (Enterprise anchor): 20% platform fee credit over 12 months + 50% retainer->credits + 2 emergency on-call rotations included for first 6 months — revenue impact: ~18% ARR concession; requires approval from Head of Sales / Finance.

Risk notes: allowing credits that apply to consumption can reduce billed MRR but preserves committed capacity. If we over-credit implementation retainer we lose runway on SRE allocation forecasting.

Ask: Ben / David, can you quickly confirm whether Option B needs CFO sign-off or if Head of Sales can approve up to 20% ARR-equivalent concessions? Also — attach MA Plan v3 for reference.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: ma-plan-v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 67KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>
Cc: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 08:21:09 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: Hearthwell concession sizing (RDW-2026-1193)

Quick reply — Finance will approve up to a 15% ARR-equivalent concession at Sales Head level. Anything >15% needs CFO review. For structured amortization we can treat the credited platform fee as a contra-revenue line and amortize over 12 months for recognition purposes; legal will expect the credit mechanics in the SOW.

David: re on-call, including two emergency rotations for 6 months is operationally heavy; cost is ~USD 48k for those rotations (est.). If we push blended P1/P2 with guaranteed 4-hour response for P1 during business hours and 8-hour for after-hours we meet most pilot needs and keep cost neutral.

Marissa — go ahead and present Option A and a slightly trimmed Option B (cap concession to ~15%) to the customer. Call out that any >15% will need CFO approval, which will add 5-7 business days. I'll draft the revenue memo for signature.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales (North America) | Redwood Inference

Hi Toby / Sally — thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the MPA note. Per internal alignment, please find two commercial options below. Both preserve committed capacity and offer the cash-smoothing you requested.

Option 1 — Pilot (recommended)
- Platform fee: 40% credit applied evenly across the first 12 monthly invoices.
- Implementation retainer: 30% converted to support credits (usable within 12 months of go-live).
- Support: Standard P1/P2 with 4-hour business-hours response; after-hours P1 escalation on a best-effort basis.
- Requirements: 4-node committed pool, baseline 120M tokens/month minimum.
- Next step: Sign SOW + SOW addendum describing credit mechanics.

Option 2 — Anchor (accelerated SLA)
- Platform fee: 20% credit over 12 months (monthly invoice credit).
- Implementation retainer: 50% converted to support credits (12-month expiration).
- Support: Includes two emergency on-call rotations for first 6 months (adds operational scheduling).
- Note: This option approaches our 15% ARR concession ceiling; any concession beyond that requires CFO sign-off and ~5 business days for approval.

We can draft the SOW addendum and credit schedule once you confirm which option you prefer. If helpful, happy to set a short call this week to walk procurement through the mechanics.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
T: +1 650 555 0123
